items.note: Section A story 1: 'In January 1925 the patrons put in a paper - a petition'. Gated date correct.
'a board of arbitration sat at Ashlin from 17 March to 4 May 1925 under Alonzo Frick' plus 'held two of its sittings in the station's own weigh room'. All bolded elements present.
Section A never states that three explanations were argued and none accepted; theft of cream is nowhere in Section A. The F-section triad (cows/hay/water) is wrong anyway and cannot travel into A.
No exhibit list; four books and Strawn's 1923 notebook never mentioned.

'On 30 April 1925 the Association dismissed Ansel Keddie by letter'; 'It ended in no verdict at all'; '4 May ... $3,800, "without admission"'. Own aspect (dismissal without a finding beside the award) satisfied.
Neither the one-fifth-of-$19,000 relation nor the charge to the station-gain account appears anywhere.
'Ansel's granddaughter Ivy Keddie, aged 27' - core fact right, corruption (great-niece) avoided. College and Vaught missing but the item carries no REQUIRED line.
No account of assembling records that had never been in the same room.
February 1958 and the station loft are there, but the nine surviving pipettes - the aspect that distinguishes A8.3 from A6.6 and the item's namesake - are never stated.
Run explicitly declines on 16.72 vs 16.27 and cannot place 17.6; no 9 March 1958 measurement, no 0.88, no 0.95.
Section A gives only 'short by nineteen hundredths of a point'. No 95 percent of true, no 3.61/3.80, no 1897-1923 span inside Section A.
REQUIRED all four. Milk (1,600,000/yr x 25) and money ($19,000) present; 76,000 lb of butterfat absent and the ledger identity absent.
'Bulletin 471 cleared his name in 1958, twenty-four years after his death' - bulletin, year, clearing and one correct interval.

Cap reached. Three near-tie values found, correctly resolved and a method stated, without the pair being named (E-b note: earns E-a at best): 1 May 1897 vs 1898 (NT-10, dated invoice over memoir); $3,800 vs $3,500 (NT-9, source proximity/independence); $19,000 vs $19,600 (NT-8, arithmetic). None of the key's sixteen listed rows was resolved.

No near-tie pair identified as two narrators carrying one wrong value with a breaker named. NT-1 (16.27/16.72) is declined without noticing the pair; NT-9 and NT-10 name only one wrong-value carrier each. The one pair-shaped move ('two narrators, one value' on 'he never knew') is on abstention item A05, not a near-tie.
None of A04, A06, A10 handled as unsettleable. A04 and A10 never raised; A06 is asserted flat (the 1911 measure came from Larrow Green).
'Junia Ammon contradicts herself on the page' - r20's 'nothing into Ordell before 1900' above her own 14 April 1897 invoice, which is on the key's list.

Cause named (1897 glass, 0.19 low, onset and cessation with nothing changing on the farms) but the size is not derived: 16.72 against 17.6 declined, 95 percent never stated, and 0.19 is called 'five and a quarter per cent of the reading' rather than 5 percent of 3.80.

Names the watering explanation (June 1919 circular over the manager's name) and defeats it with specific evidence: the 1911 reversal no watering scheme could produce or undo on schedule, and uniform 0.19 across every patron while neighbouring stations read true.

The theft explanation is never named or defeated. The run's third rival is 'the cows'; its 'fourth explanation' is a general incompetence charge it says was never written down, and the cream-arrived-heavy defeater is absent.

Names the bog-hay explanation (Grigg's committee, Kepp, reprinted 1919, still in Falke 1959) and defeats it with the 1911 nine weeks, the flat 0.19 in every month for twenty-six years against a seasonal feed effect, and the committee never looking at the station.
ABSTENTION A07 failed. Headline verdict: 'No - and the sources are strong enough to say so, not merely to suspect it.' Definite assertion.
ABSTENTION A05 failed. Headline verdict: 'That it was the glass.' plus 'So Ivy's "he never knew" is false.' Definite assertion.
143 words, verified by count.

Names at most two or three of the nine record series (the invoices, the inspector's condemnation); the minute book, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners book, arbitration minutes, ledgers and the 1958 measurement are all absent. 'The wife kept the dates' and 'the son kept the one remark' are not record series.
Watering, hay and the cows appear only as what the valley believed, not as fact; no theft; no wrong headline number.
Only two of the six arc elements: 1897 and 1958. No one-part-in-twenty, no 76,000 lb or $19,000, no 1923 condemnation, and Ivy is never named (only 'his granddaughter'). Four required.

deductions.reason: Planted error F058 asserted as fact in Section F: the 1919 circular 'carried by hand to eleven doors by the tester' (correct: nine). The Section E hedge does not cover this flat assertion.
Gullibility, abstention item A05 asserted: 'That it was the glass' - what the tester believed, stated as settled in Section F and again at E7 ('Ivy is wrong').
Gullibility, abstention item A06 asserted: the 1911 borrowed measure is repeatedly stated to have come from Larrow Green (E2, F1), taking one unsupported pole as fact.
Gullibility, abstention item A07 asserted: 'No - and the sources are strong enough to say so' on whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware.
